report:
Freshly reviewed the complete parse.detail_firewall claim, four ordinary implementation associations, the ordinary twelve-case edit test, and the explicit TODO verification entry. Captured supporting rooted-storage equality, item-relative span construction, associated-member copying, fixture setup, observer identity, query execution logging, and both linked architectural rationales. No production edits.

LocalFnSym stores name/scope/owner as identity fields while CST and absolute span are tracked details. LocalModSym similarly separates name/edition/parent identity from body source, attributes and absolute span, with membership in a separate query. parse_str_to_cst dispatches item constructors rather than placing all module syntax in one shared returned value. parse_fn creates a fresh Stash, parses declaration/body coordinates relative to its item start, roots that syntax in Stashed, and passes its absolute span separately. Other item constructors in associated items.rs likewise establish separate rooted syntax stores for represented definitions; modules and imports retain separate attribute/import details. Captured associated.rs copies each minted function/type/const member into its own item stash rather than publishing owner-stash pointers as the member product. Captured util.rs keeps relative coordinates independent of absolute source placement. Stashed equality compares a rooted fingerprint rather than allocation identity, allowing rebuilt equal siblings to backdate independently.

The current associated mods.rs change exposes symbol_local_item for final import checking and adds an association; it does not modify LocalModSym identity/detail fields, parsing, or stash ownership. The claim does not promise parsing avoids rereading the containing file; it promises identity/detail separation and per-definition products.

The ordinary test detail_edits_preserve_local_symbol_query_keys covers function body, struct field, enum payload, trait member signature, impl member body, alias target, const/static values, module doc attributes, use target, macro-definition output and macro invocation tokens. Each fixture uses a persistent Database and SourceFile setter, rejects Error items, observes the semantic symbol, checks a warm empty query log, edits source and checks that observe_symbol_identity did not execute again. Captured setup_root_module genuinely reparses/specifies membership. The observer is tracked on an interned Symbol-only key, and the captured WillExecute logging/drain implementation makes the no-reexecution assertion meaningful evidence for unchanged identity. It intentionally does not establish detail-content equivalence or downstream detail-consumer cache behavior.

The modules_parse_detail_firewall TODO correctly retains moves, sibling insertion/reordering, affected/unaffected CST fingerprints and downstream reexecution, including generated items. Its prerequisite is persistent multi-item and generated-item fixtures observing identity and detail consumers independently. The existing single-item identity tests are substantive partial evidence, not completion of that matrix. No N/A evidence applies.

Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib detail_edits_preserve_local_symbol_query_keys: 1 passed (all twelve internal cases), no failures. Source inspection accounts for all four associated implementation entries; test assertions and visible TODO account for remaining verification limits. No edits requested.
